newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares correct 1.23pct, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares correct 1.23pct, seen stabilising.

text.p: Greek equities ended 1.23 percent lower on heavy volume with market analysts saying the general share index was stabilising after big fluctuations in the last four sessions. Monday is a market holiday.

"The market's strong rise and steep fall were overreactions. On Friday, fluctuations were smaller and this is a sign of the market consolidating short-term," said analyst John Haveles, at Delphi Mutual Funds.
Volume continues to be strong and index movements will become smoother and milder. This sets the stage for a heathier market rise, he added.
"I expect the index to move in the range of 1,200 to 1,400 points until April. The new resistance level will be at 1,453 points," he said.
Further news of interest rate cuts along with easing inflation will have a positive effect on Greek equities, he said.
If May's inflation forecast proves to be accurate, below 6.0 percent, new capital will flow into the market.
Greece's consumer price inflation fell to 6.6 percent year-on-year in February from 6.8 percent in January.
Also, Athens was selected among the five candidate cities to host the Olympics 2004 Games. The other cities were Buenos Aires, Rome, Stockholm and Cape Town.
Both news were released after the market's close.
Haveles expected news of Athens' candidacy to have a mediocre effect on construction shares, because most big infrastructure projects were already under way.
The Athens general share index ended 1.23 percent or 16.41 points lower at 1319.19 points from Thursday's 1335.60, after opening at 1339.42.
Turnover was 23.0 billion drachmas on volume of 5.7 million shares. Decliners led advancers 144 to 70 with 26 issues unchanged on 240 traded.
Banking shares ended 1.44 percent lower. Construction lost 0.61 percent and industrials ended 1.34 percent down.
Investment stocks lost 2.05 percent. Leasing shares dropped 2.49 percent up and small-caps lost 1.47 percent.
